title: Native and returning-user login
prerequisites: Required: run sdk_native_preflight against the selected environment before building or activation. Native KSSIDP uses BDDKEnrollment/BDDKLogin, useTokenBasedLogin=true, astServerBackend=maverick and login header X-KOBIL-ASTUSERID. The WebView alternative is KSTrustedWebView with explicit deployment clients. Missing clients or incompatible bindings block progress; never create substitute flows.
These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
SDK started; selected local user is known.
Existing native-compatible deployment client and supported authentication mode selected.
sequence: Read current SDK/user state rather than assuming the last app session is still authenticated.
Start the selected user login through the native IDP integration.
Supply only requested credentials/challenges and route all intermediate results.
Verify SDK login completion before enabling authenticated actions.
Test return after app restart separately from initial activation; do not silently reactivate on login failure.
expected_result: Activated user can log in after restarting the app.
checklist: Activated user can log in after restarting the app.
Wrong PIN/password returns a usable error.
User identity is preserved and not confused with another local user.
failure_handling: A successful token request or webpage is not sufficient proof of SDK login.
Different SDK generations use different wrappers; match the shipped headers/API.
Never disable useTokenBasedLogin to work around ast_login_with_unactivated_client; this skips IAM setup and can cause CannotAcquireTokenData(50). Investigate the selected native backend flow instead.

Swift: switch on KssIdpStatus.success/eventFailed/requestFailed; never infer success from text containing accept. Preserve detailed callback status, errorCode and underlying event without logging tokens or credentials.

Interactive trusted WebView returning login follows the same redirect-interception and single-use authorization-code contract as activation (verified 2026-09-29, MCSDK 15.16): validate scheme/host/effective port/path plus state, consume once, and match the delivered native callback signatures (Android TWVClient POST-redirect limitation; all iOS KsTrustedWebViewDelegate methods required).

BIOMETRIC prompt timing varies by delivered SDK, platform and effective key policy. Physical-device validation has observed prompts at activation and cold OfflineLogin, while another native run completed activation without a prompt. Announce possible owner authentication before activation or protected credential/key access, leave physical prompts untouched, and record the actual prompt and SDK result separately. Absence of a prompt alone does not prove that keys are unbound: check effective policy, key state and platform authentication reuse before classifying enforcement. Selected AuthenticationMode, observed physical authentication and grant type are separate evidence claims.

OfflineLoginEvent does not by itself identify the grant. On the inspected KSMasterController source, a cached valid access token is reused; otherwise a refresh token is tried. If both are unavailable, the selected first factor is SignedJWT only when the effective SDK configuration has maverick.jwtSignKeySecurityPolicy and the auth mode is not password; without that policy, the SDK selects the offline-token factor. The effective policy is loaded at SDK Start from configuration. Verify it through an approved, redacted configuration review; never print a signed configuration or token. Source reviewed in source file, source file and source file; qualify this behavior against the delivered SDK version.

Safe SignedJWT diagnostic, only after the policy and non-password auth mode are confirmed: ClearIamTokenCacheEvent with CLEAR_ACCESS_AND_REFRESH, then OfflineLoginEvent and GetIamAccessTokenClaimsEvent. This preserves the separate offline token. Require a sanitized SDK diagnostic showing the jwt-bearer grant or equivalent issuer evidence; fresh iat, OfflineLogin success, or biometric prompt alone is insufficient because offline-token refresh also issues a fresh token. If the effective policy or grant evidence is unavailable, report NOT_PROVEN. Never use CLEAR_ALL for this test: it also deletes the offline token and can cause NO_TOKEN_DATA_AVAILABLE, as observed in round 4. Never print tokens or full claims; retain only approved, non-sensitive metadata.

SignedJWT switch: mc_config maverick.jwtSignKeySecurityPolicy with one of ENFORCE_STRONG_HARDWARE, ENFORCE_HARDWARE, ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD (source file: unknown values fail config parsing). The SDK stores the policy at Start and the signing key is created at activation, so the policy must be present BEFORE the user is activated; adding it later requires a new activation. Without the key, useTokenBasedLogin=true alone gives the offline-token refresh path, which round-4 workers mistook for the signed-JWT login (measured 2026-10-02: ClearIamTokenCache access+refresh -> OfflineLogin served by the offline token; CLEAR_ALL -> NO_TOKEN_DATA_AVAILABLE).

Signed-JWT proof signature (measured 2026-10-02/05, SDK 15.16, IDP core 8.0.x, hardware-backed and software-backed signing keys): with jwtSignKeySecurityPolicy set before activation, ClearIamTokenCacheEvent(CLEAR_ACCESS_AND_REFRESH) then OfflineLoginEvent prompts for the device biometric and returns OK; the decrypted SDK log shows event GetIamAccessTokenUsingJwtBearer followed by the realm token-endpoint POST and 'Success 200' under the same request uuid, and the IDP core log shows, in one trace, 'Entered into JWT_BEARER_GRANT_TYPE request' -> 'AST Client login succeeded!' -> 'JWT:GRANT::Token Verification Successful' (JWTGrantTypeFunctions). Without that log line (or the equivalent realm LOGIN event with grant type jwt-bearer) report the grant as NOT_PROVEN, whatever the SDK status says. Side effect to plan for when activation ran through a separate enrollment client: the token issued by this grant belongs to that enrollment client (claims azp), so after every cold start with OfflineLogin an explicit-auth TMS needs one interactive login with the token client first (verify claims azp == token client); ordinary TMS does not. If activation and login use the same client this does not apply.

Sign-key policy versus target (measured SDK 15.16, 2026-10-02/05): ENFORCE_STRONG_HARDWARE and ENFORCE_HARDWARE need a StrongBox/TEE or Secure Enclave key and FAIL on Android emulators (Start NOT_SUPPORTED status 46 / 800000278, isKeyInsideSecureHardware securityLevel 0) and iOS simulators (key creation Secure Enclave -25293, LocalAuthentication -1020, SDK 802025293). ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD works on both with a software-backed key (jwt-bearer grant + token HTTP 200 measured) and keeps a hardware key on physical devices. Resolve target and policy BEFORE the first activation: on an emulator/simulator with an ENFORCE_* policy stop, explain, and offer ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD for the test fixture or a physical device; never downgrade a deployment policy silently and never consume an activation code into a known failure.

NOT_SUPPORTED at Start is not proof that the device lacks secure hardware: the same status appeared on a physical device when the Android CSR helper could not load JcaContentSignerBuilder (missing org.bouncycastle:bcpkix-jdk15to18). Read the native log lines isKeyInsideSecureHardware / GetKeystoreInfo before attributing the cause.

What a target can prove: emulator/simulator = protocol truth (Start, activation, WebView login, claims, ordinary and explicit TMS, archive, and the SignedJWT grant path with ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD - the only target that exercises the software-key fallback). Physical device = key-protection and biometric truth (securityLevel, StrongBox/Secure Enclave, STRONG biometric class without credential fallback). Record the target with every result; a software-key pass does not qualify a hardware-only deployment and a hardware pass does not prove the virtual fallback.

Agent duty: the MCP user must not fail on a target or realm configuration they could not know. Before activation run sdk_deployment_preflight with require_signed_jwt=true when SignedJWT is intended; before the first explicit TMS run sdk_tms_explicit_preflight(token_client, enrollment_client) and report missing preconditions as a realm configuration item for that realm's owner (never fix a customer realm from a test run); after a cold OfflineLogin re-check the azp claim before an explicit TMS. On failure name the measured cause (target, policy, realm configuration) and the one change the user has to make.

platform_notes.android: NativeLoginViewModel and SubsequentLoginViewModel are separate entry points.
platform_notes.ios: KssIdpModel.login passes an explicitly chosen client/auth mode and may carry the selected user ID header.

qualification.note: Examples compile against the exact classic MCSDK/KSSIDP artifact in each example validation record. Compilation and synthetic diagnostics do not qualify a complete live app flow.
